children: U.S. soybean futures fell on Wednesday, pressured by a decline in crude oil prices, after rising more than 2% in the previous session on a slower-than-expected August soybean crush rate.
Wheat and corn also edged lower.
FUNDAMENTALS
* The most-active soybean contract
on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) was down 0.13% at $13.17 a bushel, as of 0042 GMT.
* Wheat
lost 0.41% to $7.25-1/2 a bushel and corn
dropped 0.14% to $5.35 a bushel.

* Oil prices fell after an unexpected build in U.S. crude inventories, while investors assessed supply risks after Saudi Arabia suspended oil loadings at its Yanbu port. Soybeans and corn often track crude oil prices because of their use in biofuel production.

* Soybean prices were supported in the previous session by gains in soymeal after the National Oilseed Processors Association reported that its members crushed 205.456 million bushels of soybeans in August, an 11-month low, while soyoil stocks fell to their lowest level since November 2024.
* Harvesting was underway across the U.S. Midwest, although heavy rain was delaying fieldwork in parts of Iowa, the nation's largest corn producer and second-largest soybean producer.

* Brazilian crop agency Conab forecast the country's 2026/27 soybean production at 181.64 million metric tons, up 0.7% from the previous year but below the U.S. Department of Agriculture's current forecast for Brazil of 186 million tons.
* Traders assessed risks to grain exports from the Black Sea region following further attacks on infrastructure.
* Algeria's state grains agency OAIC bought about 500,000 tons of milling wheat in an international tender that closed on Tuesday, European traders said.
* Ahead of a Statistics Canada crop report due on Wednesday, analysts surveyed by Reuters on average expected the agency to estimate Canada's 2026 all-wheat harvest at 36.73 million tons.
* Commodity funds were net buyers of CBOT corn, soy and wheat futures, traders said on Tuesday. (CBOT/FUNDS)
